title: Anchor-status standoff: a consumer repolls anchors K reports as terminally failed — K's labelling is already honest (KS-587), so the fix is terminal-state handling, not a new K signal
description:
## BLUF

**The standoff is real, but its stated mechanism is wrong — and measuring demo inverted the ownership.** The premise going in was *"K reports simulated anchors as* `confirmed`*; Platform S's honesty rule refuses a* `mock_tx_` *hash; S repolls forever."* Measured on demo tonight, **K does not report them as confirmed.** All 83 simulated anchors on demo are flagged `simulated = true`, `status = failed`, carrying the explicit error `KS-587: simulated placeholder — never on chain; marked …`. **Zero rows on demo are** `simulated = true` **and** `confirmed`**.** K already fixed this — that is what **KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587** were.

So the accurate statement is: **a consumer is polling anchors that K reports as terminally** `failed`**, forever.** That is not a labelling defect on our side. It is a missing terminal-state rule on the consumer side.

## Recommendation

1. **Layer 1 — the actual fix, PS-side (Stuart's):** treat `status: failed` as **terminal** and stop polling. No new K signal is required; the one already published is sufficient and has been since KS-587 deployed.
2. **Layer 2 — K exposes** `simulated` **machine-readably: ALREADY DONE. This is a no-op, closed here, and no work should be raised for it.** Verified in the **shipped** demo image, not just the source tree.
3. **Layer 3 — env hygiene (Stuart's call):** whatever is polling demo from `52.74.18.212` should not be pointed at demo at all.
4. **Layer 4 — per-environment Blockfrost keys:** still open, still pending the credential question below.

## Detail — what was measured, on demo, read-only

**Demo is not simulating.** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is **absent** from the anchoring container's environment (0 matches against a 22-line env, so the read itself is proven). Boot logs: `Cardano integration active — real blockchain anchoring enabled`, `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"`, network `preview`.

`anchor_store` **composition — 285 rows total:**

| shape | `simulated` | `status` | n | first | last |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| real 64-hex | false | **confirmed** | **194** | 2026-07-08 | 2026-08-14 |
| `mock_tx_*` | **true** | **failed** | **83** | 2026-07-31 | 2026-08-01 |
| NULL | false | failed | 6 | 2026-07-11 | 2026-08-05 |
| real 64-hex | false | failed | 2 | 2026-08-04 | 2026-08-10 |

Crosstab, stated plainly because it is the whole argument: `simulated = true` appears **only** with `status = failed`. **There is no (**`simulated = true`**,** `confirmed`**) row on demo.** Controls: `simulated` is never NULL (0 of 285); totals reconcile 194 + 83 + 6 + 2 = 285.

**The loop's corpus is fully resident on demo — the cross-instance hypothesis is dead.** All **71** distinct anchor ids the loop requests are present in demo's `anchor_store`: **71 present / 0 absent**. Controls both fired: a fabricated id `anchor_0000…0000` matched **0**, a known-real id matched **1**. So these anchors were minted **on demo**; they were not minted on a simulated instance elsewhere and verified here.

**And every one of them is a failed anchor:**

|  | n |
| -- | -- |
| `simulated = true`, `failed`, mock hash | **68** |
| `simulated = false`, `failed`, NULL hash | **3** |
| **confirmed** | **0** |

That is the finding. The loop is polling **71 anchors that can never succeed**, 68 of which K has explicitly labelled as simulated placeholders that were never on chain.

**The** `simulated` **flag is machine-readable, and it ships.** In the **running** demo image (`/app/dist/index.js`, and `docker inspect` shows **no bind-mounts**, so the image *is* what serves):

* `...(simulated ? { simulated: true, simulatedTxRef: rawTxHash } : {})` — 3 emit sites
* `verified: !txView.simulated && anchor.status === 'confirmed'`
* a placeholder hash is moved to `simulatedTxRef` and `transactionHash` is set to **null**, so a mock hash is never presented as a transaction hash

Control: a nonsense token grepped for in the same file returned 0. Source agrees (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `honestTxView`, `anchoring.openapi.ts` `simulated: z.boolean().optional()` + `simulatedTxRef`).

**The Blockfrost split — both "zero Blockfrost calls" and "quota exhausted" are true at once.** They describe **different routes**:

| route | behaviour | last 60 min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` | **pure DB read**, ~1 ms, no Blockfrost | **1,970 × 200** |
| `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` | **live Blockfrost** | **608 × 200 · 460 × 500** |

**457** of those 500s carry Blockfrost's own string `"Usage is over limit."` (against 3,935 total anchoring log lines). So Stuart's agent's *"zero Blockfrost calls in two hours"* is **correct for status GETs** — that is exactly what they observed, and it is a real property of the code. Our *"quota exhausted"* is **correct for verify-by-hash**. Neither observation refutes the other; the earlier reconciliation hypothesis (creation-simulated / verify-live) was the right shape but the wrong axis — it is **status-read vs verify-by-hash**, not creation vs verification.

**Traffic, for scale.** Last 6 h at demo's edge: **23,515 requests from** `52.74.18.212`**, of 23,515 total — 100.0%** of demo's inbound. Split: `POST /api/verification/verify` 11,620 · `GET /api/anchors/{id}` 9,704 · `GET /api/documents/{id}` 2,190 — **all 200 at the gateway.** ~3,919/hr, consistent with the ~3,850/hr measured on KS-670 across 08-14 → 08-21.

## Attribution, corrected gently

Stuart's agent read the honesty rule as **S's**. The record says the honest-labelling rule was implemented **in K**: **KS-520** (Urgent, Done) — anchoring fabricated a `tx_sim_` hash and marked the document anchored under `SIMULATE_ANCHORING`; **KS-522** (High, Done) — a simulated anchor presented as genuinely verified, no honest-labelling signal; **KS-587** (High, Deployed to UAT) — *"84 demo anchors carry* `mock_tx_` *hashes but are flagged* `simulated=false` *+ confirmed"*. KS-587 is the direct ancestor of this ticket: it found **84** mis-flagged rows and remediated them. Tonight demo holds **83** rows carrying its remediation message. **The defect Stuart's agent describes is one K already found and fixed** — which is worth saying clearly, because it means no K change is needed and the polling behaviour is unaffected by anything we ship.

Credit where due: their diagnosis of the *mechanism* — a consumer refusing a mock hash and retrying forever — is correct and is what made this tractable. Only the direction of the labelling defect was off, and their own caveat (which K instance they queried was unstated) is what prompted the measurement that found it.

## What their numbers describe

Their **1,638 anchors, all simulated** is **not demo** — demo has **285** anchors, of which 83 are simulated. Since all 71 polled ids resolve on demo, the polling target is demo; the 1,638-row instance they inspected is a different K (most likely one of the local development stacks). **Not asserted, and it does not change the finding:** the fix is terminal-state handling regardless of which K holds the larger simulated corpus.

## Still open

* **The credential question, unanswered since 2026-08-20:** does the local K stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key or its own? If demo's, per-environment key scoping becomes the durable fix, and Kintsugi (its own free-tier project per environment) is the working precedent.
* **The Blockfrost allowance *period* is still unverified** — nothing here should be sized on a 50k/day assumption.

## Provenance

* Demo measurements | read-only SSH to `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-08-21 10:26–10:40Z | container env, `docker logs`, `psql` SELECTs, and one `docker inspect`. **No writes, no config change, no key action, no restarts.** Two scratch files created under the VM's `/tmp` during extraction were removed in the same command.
* Loop corpus | demo nginx gateway logs, 6 h window | two of my own extraction patterns were wrong on the first pass (`doc_` vs `doc-`, and verify hashes ride in the POST body rather than the URL); both corrected before any figure here was written down.
* KS-520 / KS-522 / KS-587 / PS-522 | live Linear reads, 2026-08-21 | `PS-522` returns nothing; `KS-999` used as a not-found control.

nodes.body:
## Confirmed at demo's edge — the loop is gone, and the slow lane left its own signature rather than just a silence

## BLUF

@stuart.jamieson — **measured on demo, your fix works, and the evidence is better than "the traffic stopped."** The loop from `52.74.18.212` has collapsed **from ~3,906 requests/hour to 60/hour**, a **98.5%** reduction, and the Blockfrost-consuming route is down **~99.9%**. More usefully: at **18:16–18:18Z** all **71** parked anchors were polled **exactly once each** — the 6-hour revisit lane firing for the first time, on schedule. That pattern is the fix running. A merely-dead process would have produced zero.

**One thing this does *not* fix, and it is ours, not yours: the Blockfrost allowance has not rolled.** Probed live just now from inside `secuura-anchoring` — demo key **402 Project Over Limit**, deliberately wrong key **403** as the control. So demo's on-chain verification is **still down**; the *cause* of the exhaustion is gone, the exhaustion itself has not lapsed yet. That is KS-670, not this ticket, and not your fix's job.

## RECOMMENDATION

Nothing needed from you here. Layer 1 is closed on the evidence below. What remains is ours (KS-670's quota recovery), yours-but-separate (**Layer 3** — the residual poller below), and still-open (**Layer 4**).

---

## The measurement

Instrument unchanged from the sessions before this one: demo's nginx gateway log, whole-loop rate by hour, plus the corpus. Buffer covers **2026-08-14T05:06:59Z → 2026-08-21T20:17:30Z**, so the window is fully inside the retained log — no clipping.

| window | requests/hour from `52.74.18.212` |
| -- | -- |
| 20 Aug 15:00–23:00Z | 3,856–3,956 |
| 21 Aug 00:00–11:00Z | 3,390–3,957 |
| **21 Aug 13:00–19:00Z** | **60** |

Share of demo's total inbound: **100%** before, **100%** after — it is still the only caller, just a vastly quieter one.

By route, the part that matters for the quota:

| route | before (per hour) | after (7 hours total) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/verification/verify` — the Blockfrost-backed path | ~1,930 | **17** |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` — DB read | ~1,560 | **71** |
| `GET /api/documents/{id}` — DB read | ~350 | 432 |

## 🔴 A correction to my own first reading, because it changes the attribution

My first pass read the collapse as **12:51Z** from hourly buckets and I nearly wrote that down. At minute resolution it is **12:17Z** — the 12:00 bucket simply held its last 17 minutes at full rate. The sequence:

- **12:17Z** — anchor GETs and verify POSTs both stop dead. Not a taper: 12:17 has 33 anchor + 5 verify, 12:18 has 0 and 0.
- **12:51Z** — the steady document poll halves, 2/min → 1/min. That is your container replacement (image built 12:48:44Z, up 12:51Z, per PS-645).
- **18:16–18:18Z** — the burst below.

So the *stop* preceded your deploy by 34 minutes, which is exactly what taking the old service down for a redeploy looks like. **The stop alone therefore proves nothing about the fix** — a killed process gives the same picture. Worth being explicit about, because it would have been easy and wrong to credit the fix with the silence.

## The evidence that *is* about the fix

| | |
| -- | -- |
| anchors polled 18:16–18:18Z | **71** |
| times each was polled | **exactly 1** — the histogram is 71 anchors × 1 poll, no other bucket |
| corroborating verifies in the same burst | 17 |
| requests in the gap 12:18Z → 18:15Z | **0**, against a control of 1,072 in the surrounding hours |
| interval from last pre-stop poll (12:16–12:17Z) | **~6h 00m** |

**That is `RefreshFailedRevisitHours` = 6 firing, and nothing else looks like it.** Each parked row revisited once and re-parked; none re-entered the fast lane. Your design description — a cadence rather than a tombstone, because PS-577 exists — is doing precisely what you said it would, and I can see the shape of it in someone else's logs, which is the nicest way to have a claim confirmed.

The 17 verifies against 71 anchors also matches your account: simulated rows park **without** corroboration, only genuine faileds pay for a chain lookup on revisit.

## PS-645 read before writing this

Your estate check closes cleanly and its uat-ps numbers reconcile with mine from the other side: **86 placeholders of which 71 are `anchor_` refs** — the same 71-anchor corpus I count at demo's gateway, independently. dev-ps empty, prod out of scope on the unexplained changed ED25519 host key. Not bypassing strict checking on a production box was the right call.

## The residual — one poller is still pointed at demo (Layer 3)

Steady, unbroken, through all of the above:

```
GET /api/documents/doc-1786170172896-935abaa5    once per minute
```

**438 of the 452 document GETs since 13:00Z are that single document id** — one document, 1/min, **~1,440 requests/day**. It is a DB read and touches no Blockfrost, so it costs demo almost nothing — but it is the whole of demo's remaining inbound traffic, and it is the concrete form of the Layer 3 question: *should that box be pointed at demo at all?* Flagging, not asking you to act today.

## Still open, and not re-asked

**Layer 4 — the credential question** (does that stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key, or its own?) remains asked and unanswered from 2026-08-20. Recording it as open; per-environment keys are still the durable fix and Kintsugi is the precedent.

---

*Measured read-only on demo: nginx and anchoring log reads, plus the two staged Blockfrost probes from inside the container. No writes, no config, no restarts. Quota state and its control recorded on KS-670.*

**Layer 1 is merged** — PS-644's slow-lane parking landed on Platform-S develop (`f29173c`, PR #581) and PS-644 is Done. Verified live before merge: 19 suite-created anchors all parked after one status poll each, and 0 anchor GETs + 0 verify POSTs in idle sampling where the old loop produced ~228.

Local estate update relevant to your traffic figures: the machine's last old-code poller — a host-run S from a stale worktree, up since 08-14, which was the "105 anchors / 1,638-row local K" driver — was stopped today, so this machine now contributes zero anchor polling to any K.

**Unchanged and still yours/Stuart's:** the 52.74.18.212→demo loop continues until the fix deploys to that environment (S-side deploys are manual while GitHub Actions billing is dead), your Layer 3 (whether that box should point at demo at all) and Layer 4 (per-environment Blockfrost keys + the 2026-08-20 credential question), and the estate check now tracked on PS-645.

Layer 1 is implemented on Platform-S: https://github.com/Secuura/platform-s/pull/581 (PS-644, In Review).

Your measurement reshaped the fix, so recording what changed because of it:

- **`failed` is now effectively terminal — as a cadence, not a tombstone.** Rows last observed failed/simulated leave the fast lane for `RefreshFailedRevisitHours` (default 6 h) and re-enter by themselves. We kept a slow-lane revisit rather than a hard stop deliberately: PS-577 exists because 91 UAT anchors sat "failed" on the anchors endpoint while your verify reported them confirmed with real hashes — if K's reconcile ever heals a row again, S still collects it, just hours later instead of never.
- **Your Blockfrost split is what killed the corroboration cost.** Since status GETs are pure DB reads and verify-by-hash is the Blockfrost-backed route, the expensive part of S's loop was PS-577's corroborating verify on every failed poll. Simulated anchors now park **without** corroboration at all (no chain fact exists to find), and genuine faileds corroborate only on slow-lane revisits.
- **Attribution accepted:** the honest-labelling chain (KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587) is K's, and your read that the 1,638-row instance was a local dev K is right — it's the laptop stack, which predates KS-587 and still reports simulated anchors as `confirmed` + `mock_tx_`. S handles both shapes: your `simulated: true` flag first, mock-prefix fallback for older images.

Verified live on that local stack rebuilt with the fix: 19 suite-created anchors all parked after one status poll each; 3 idle minutes = **0** anchor GETs and **0** verify POSTs where the old loop produced ~228. Once this deploys to the environment behind `52.74.18.212`, the 71-anchor loop against demo should collapse the same way — your Layer 3 (whether that box should point at demo at all) and Layer 4 (per-environment Blockfrost keys, plus the credential question from 2026-08-20) remain open for Stuart.
